touches.text: Code that is no longer needed is deleted. Git history keeps it if we ever need it back.

WHY: Law 8: nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass, and the verdict must come from a hand the builder did not guide. A green cannot be self-granted. A machine under CodeMother, not a device: CodeMother does not build, so the tester inside her puts no builder between a build and its verdict, and nothing here needs its own process in the rack, since each proof run is its own process already.
Runs a proof as its own process and writes a validation record (claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, falsifier, horizon).
Hollow runs: proves a proof goes red when the build is removed.
Seals: one current validation per proof, beside the proof. A seal holds while the code it measured is unchanged.
